job.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Frontier Engineering
job._content:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


FORWARD DEPLOYED ENGINEER, FRONTIER ENGINEERING

Snowflake is about empowering enterprises to achieve their full potential – and people too. With a culture that's all in on impact, innovation, and collaboration, Snowflake is the sweet spot for building big, moving fast, and taking technology – and careers – to the next level.

Where Data Does More. Join the Snowflake team.

At Snowflake, we are building a high-impact team to help the world's most innovative companies unlock the power of AI. As a Forward Deployed Engineer on our Frontier Engineering team, you will be a hands-on builder and a key technical partner to our most strategic customers, placing you at the forefront of the enterprise AI revolution. You won't just work with cutting-edge technology – you'll deploy it to solve real-world business problems at scale, building production-grade AI systems using Snowpark, Cortex, and our native LLM capabilities.


IN THIS ROLE AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

Build Customer Solutions: Architect, build, and deploy enterprise-grade AI solutions, including sophisticated AI agents. Own the end-to-end lifecycle of your workstreams – from prototype to production – directly solving customers' most complex business challenges.

Own the Quality of What You Ship: Define what "good" means for the systems you build. Translate ambiguous customer goals into measurable quality metrics, evaluation frameworks, and golden datasets – then run systematic eval loops to hill-climb on agent quality, catch regressions before customers do, and continuously raise the bar on accuracy, faithfulness, and safety. Treat measurement as a first-class part of building, not an afterthought.

Deliver with Velocity: Rapidly design, iterate, and ship high-quality code and pipelines. Translate ambiguous business objectives into robust, scalable, and performant solutions using Python and SQL.

Productionize AI at Scale: Own the full implementation lifecycle for your solutions – from prototype through deployment, monitoring, and optimization in secure, large-scale production environments. Build the safety guardrails, observability, and human-review workflows that keep AI applications reliable and trustworthy, and close the loop from production traces and user feedback back into your evals so quality compounds over time.

Be a Technical Partner: Partner directly with customer data science and engineering teams as a hands-on technical resource and trusted advisor on how to best leverage AI for their business challenges.

Collaborate to Innovate: Work cross-functionally with Snowflake's Product and Engineering teams, sharing real-world feedback from the field to directly influence the future of Snowflake's AI platform.

Have the opportunity to travel: Spend at least 25% of your time onsite, working closely with Snowflake's most strategic customers.


WE'RE LOOKING FOR CANDIDATES WHO HAVE:


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience.

 - Willingness to travel.

 - Proven experience building applications using LLMs, especially with technologies like RAG and agentic workflows.

 - Hands-on experience defining quality metrics and running evaluations for LLM or agent systems, and using evals to systematically improve quality.

 - Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, with an ability to articulate complex technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a desire to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing Generative AI environment.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience building eval sets from production traces and synthetic data, and running structured experimentation (A/B tests, ablations, offline evals) to compare prompts, models, or agent architectures.

 - Familiarity with eval and observability tooling (e.g., Braintrust, LangSmith, Arize, Weave, Promptfoo) or experience building custom eval harnesses.

 - Experience with failure-mode analysis on agent or RAG systems – categorizing errors (hallucination, retrieval miss, planning failure, tool misuse) and driving each down with targeted evals.

 - Hands-on experience with the MLOps lifecycle, including model deployment, monitoring, and evaluation in a cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP).

 - Familiarity with core data science libraries and tools (e.g., pandas, numpy, Snowpark).

 - Experience in a customer-facing technical role (e.g., solutions architect, sales engineer, or professional services).

 - Startup experience.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

Build the future of banking.
 
Zeta is a next-generation banking technology company providing cloud-native, fully stackable processing and core banking platforms for issuers. job._content:
what is CRED?
 
CRED is an exclusive community for India’s most trustworthy and creditworthy individuals, where the members are rewarded for good financial behavior. CRED was born out of a need to bring back the focus on a long lost virtue, one of trust, the idea being to create a community centered around this virtue. a community that constantly strives to become more virtuous in this regard till they finally scale their behavior to create a utopia where being trustworthy is the norm and not the exception. to build a community like this requires a community of its own; a community special in its own way, working towards making this vision come true. 
 
here’s a thought experiment: what do you get when you put a group of incredibly passionate and driven people and entrust them with the complete freedom to chase down their goals in a completely uninhibited manner? answer: you get something close to what we have at CRED; CRED just has it better. 
 
here’s what will be in store for you at CRED once you join as a part of the datascience fraud team:

role overview
as a fraud analyst at CRED, you’ll work at the intersection of data, technology and fraud prevention to identify and prevent emerging fraud patterns across products.
fraud patterns continue to evolve, making it important to identify and address emerging risks and vulnerabilities. you’ll think like an adversary -analyse data and system behaviour, spot unusual patterns and vulnerabilities, and work closely with data science, product and engineering teams to build practical solutions that prevent fraud.
this is a hands-on problem-solving role. you don’t need to be a fraud expert or a deep ml specialist. what matters is strong analytical and coding fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to approach problems from first principles.

SDE-III
job._content:
Who we are

Mindtickle is the market-leading revenue productivity platform that combines on-the-job learning and deal execution to drive more revenue per rep. We help revenue teams at world-class companies unleash their potential by providing a unified platform for conversation intelligence, training, coaching, and analytics. Recognized as a market leader by top industry analysts and ranked by G2 as the #1 sales onboarding and training product, Mindtickle serves a global customer base across industries, scales, and maturity levels. The engineering work behind the platform sits at the intersection of data pipelines, real-time analytics, AI-powered content and coaching intelligence, search, integrations, and platform infrastructure.

Job summary

The SDE-III is a senior technical leader inside a product team. The role is defined by scope, not tenure or technology.

SDE-IIIs own the architecture of complex systems that span the user interface, the services behind it, and the data underneath. They take a problem from an ambiguous customer need to a running system, keep it healthy in production, and make the engineers around them better.

This is not a mid-level engineer with a different title. The role exists for people who own designs and their outcomes, not only the implementation of someone else's design.

This is a lateral hire. The person joins the engineering organization and any product team can take them, so the role is described by scope and stack, not by one team's roadmap.

Key responsibilities

Own the architecture of complex systems — take a problem from an ambiguous need to a running system across front end, services and data. Make the structural decisions, write down the trade-offs, and stay accountable for how the system behaves months later.

Deliver end to end. Break down large initiatives, lead them across the stack, and ship reliably. Keep pull requests focused and reviewable.

Own the operational health of the systems your team runs. Improve observability, lead post-mortems, reduce incident frequency, and drive performance work with measured outcomes.

Lead technically beyond your own team. Lead design reviews, including for systems you do not own. Resolve competing technical approaches. Influence through clarity, not authority.

Make other engineers better — through design reviews, technical mentorship, and creating clarity in areas where others are stuck. Distribute knowledge rather than concentrate it.

Keep systems simple over time. Deprecate what no longer earns its cost. Choose the boring option where it suffices.

Understand the customer. Know why a feature exists, who uses it, and how customer configuration varies. Push back on flawed requirements.

Use AI as part of everyday engineering — writing and reviewing code, generating tests, debugging, documenting — and have the judgment to say where an AI-native approach should replace or augment a traditional one, and where it should not.

Required qualifications

Clear evidence of significant industry experience as an individual contributor in software engineering, with the most recent years operating at SDE-III scope or equivalent. Scope is defined by the kind of problem owned, not the title held.

Full-stack delivery in production. Systems you built and shipped across the user interface and the services and data behind it, and stayed responsible for afterwards.

Demonstrated architectural ownership. Evidence that you made structural decisions, not only implemented them: designed systems from scratch, led significant refactors, or evaluated technology choices, with the trade-offs.

Production discipline. Direct ownership of systems running in production, with demonstrated work on reliability, observability, or operational improvement, including diagnosing incidents and running post-mortems.

Technical influence and mentorship. Design documents or patterns that shaped decisions beyond your own team, and engineers who grew because of your mentoring.

Strong written technical communication. Design documents or technical proposals that articulate trade-offs in writing.

Judgment on complexity. A record of making systems simpler — deprecations led, abstractions removed, boring technology chosen where it sufficed.

Fluency with AI coding assistants. Daily use to build, review, test, and document, with a specific account of where they help and where they mislead.

Strong programming ability in our stack: React on the front end, and a back end in Go primarily, with Java or Python also in use. Services run on AWS.

Preferred qualifications

Experience in B2B SaaS, multi-tenant systems, workflow-heavy platforms, or integration-heavy architectures, where customer variation and backward compatibility are first-class constraints.

Led a migration, deprecation, or platform investment that reduced long-term technical cost.

Performance work with measured outcomes on both the client and the server.

Hands-on experience with AWS services, containers, and CI/CD.

Go as a primary back-end language.

Evidence of evaluating AI-native approaches for product problems, with a decision and a reason.

Published technical writing — engineering blog posts, design documents, RFCs, or conference talks with substantive material.

Familiarity with the broader Mindtickle problem space — sales enablement, revenue productivity, learning systems, content intelligence, or call analytics.

job.title: AI Native Builder - Frontend
job._content:
WHO WE ARE

Atlan is building the context layer for enterprise AI. Enterprises are pouring money into AI and most of it dies in production because the AI does not understand the business context around the data. That is the problem Atlan solves.

Gartner has named context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and calls context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents, naming Atlan one of three vendors already building it. We are also the only vendor named a Leader across all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the foundation the context layer runs on.

Come build the infrastructure that AI runs on.


THE TEAM

You'll work on three things together: Atlan's context layer, the platforms that make it usable, and the agents that run on top of it.

The platform handles the things agents need to be trusted in production: knowing which agents and skills exist, understanding what happened during a run, evaluating how well they performed, and controlling access and cost.

Then there are the agents themselves. Each one is built to do a specific job, either for our customers or for our own teams. These aren't demos sitting on a slide. We already have an agent our CSMs rely on, three GTM agents that replace around 3,000 manual calls, an agent that watches changes across atlan.com http://atlan.com, and an agent that monitors our other agents.

We share what we're learning through Becoming Frontier https://atlan.com/frontier/.

You'll own the frontend, but you won't be limited to the frontend. We use AI heavily in how we build, and we expect you to be comfortable working across the stack.

We work in small "two-slice" teams. You'll typically own an initiative with one or two other people. There's no large team around you to hand work off to, so you'll have a lot of ownership over how something gets built.



WHAT WILL YOU DO?

 - Take a 0→1 idea all the way to production. Figure out the problem, write the spec when one doesn't exist, make the architecture decisions and build it.

 - Own the frontend experience for agents. Build the interfaces people use to find, run, inspect and approve agents. Care about rendering performance and build components that other engineers can build on.

 - Work beyond the frontend. Use coding agents to navigate unfamiliar backend code, make changes and validate their output rather than blindly trusting what they generate.

 - Build agents with the people who will actually use them. Demo early, learn from real usage and put the agent into the workflow where the work already happens.

 - Design for things going wrong. Think through what happens when a tool fails, context is missing, an agent isn't confident or a human needs to take over.

 - Make agent behavior observable. Connect traces and evals to the version of the agent that produced them, and treat changes in quality as regressions worth investigating.

 - Build AI-native yourself. Use coding agents as part of your daily workflow, while keeping the engineering and architectural bar high.

 - Share what you learn. Turn useful patterns into skills, reference architectures and demos that other engineers can build on.



WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT MATCH FOR US?


MUST HAVE

 - Strong frontend fundamentals. You've shipped production UIs using React, Vue or something similar with TypeScript, and you've dealt with hard problems around rendering performance, component systems or framework migrations.

 - You've taken 0→1 products from an idea to production, often without a neatly defined spec.

 - You've shipped agents or LLM-powered systems that real people use, and can debug failures down to the context, tool call or decision that caused them.

 - You use evals to understand where agents fail and improve them based on real user impact.

 - You use coding agents regularly and hold their output to the same engineering bar as your own.

 - You're a critical optimist. You can get excited about new technology without taking it at face value, and you're comfortable reasoning from first principles.

 - You enjoy owning an initiative with a small number of people rather than working as one part of a large team.


STRONG BONUS

 - React, Vite and TypeScript, which is our current stack.

 - Experience with MCP, A2A, agent frameworks, LLM gateways or agent observability.

 - Experience as a founding engineer or working at an early-stage startup.

 - A public trail of work, such as an active GitHub, npm packages or open-source contributions, that gives us a sense of how you build.


THIS PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF...

You want to manage a large team, prefer having a well-defined backlog handed to you, only want to work on the frontend, or are still waiting to start working with AI.

We're looking for someone who wants to build with this technology now.




WHY ATLAN?

Joining Atlan means being part of a global movement to help data teams do their life’s best work. Here’s what you can expect:

 - Competitive Compensation:  We benchmark at the top of the market and keep compensation simple: strong base salary, performance‑based variable pay, and impact‑driven equity (for most roles), so your total rewards grow in step with the value you create over time.
